description: Issue #975: DistributedLookupCacheService.RefreshAsync<T> had the same structural gap #944 fixed in the sibling in-memory LookupCacheService.RefreshAsync -- its own GetAll/GetAllAsync methods both open with `if (!_registry.ContainsKey(typeof(T))) return LoadFromDb...` before touching the cache, but RefreshAsync had no equivalent check and proceeded straight to Invalidate/LoadFromDbAsync/SetDistributedAsync for ANY T, registered or not. Re-derived from THIS class's own SetDistributedAsync -> BuildCacheEntryOptions (not assumed from #944): unlike #944 (LookupCacheService.SetCache only sets a TTL when the registry lookup succeeds, so an unregistered type there got NO TTL and sat in IMemoryCache immortally), this class's BuildCacheEntryOptions falls back to a BOUNDED 30-minute TTL (`attr != null ? TimeSpan.FromMinutes(attr.TtlMinutes) : TimeSpan.FromMinutes(30)`) when the type is not in _registry -- so an unregistered type written here self-expires rather than living forever. That bounded-vs-immortal difference is why this is a separate issue (#975) instead of being folded into #944's fix, even though the missing guard itself is structurally identical. Still a real defect: writing an unregistered type bypasses the IsCacheable(typeof(T)) contract GetAll/GetAllAsync already enforce for the same type, under the same key namespace those methods deliberately skip. Reachable in production via WTMContext.RefreshLookupAsync<T>() exactly like #944 (svc.GetAttribute(typeof(T)) returns null for an unregistered type with no guard, then svc.RefreshAsync<T>(...) is called unconditionally regardless). Forced into kind='security' for the same reason lookupcache943-distributed-refreshasync-acquired-guard-neutralize.json and lookupcache944-refreshasync-registry-guard-neutralize.json document: VALID_KINDS in run_mutant.py only recognizes {'security','selftest'} and this is not a runner meta-fixture -- it is not a traditional auth/injection defect, but a cache-pollution / contract-bypass integrity guard. This mutant changes the guard `if (!_registry.ContainsKey(typeof(T)))` to `if (false)` -- a one-line, compile-preserving change that makes the bypass permanently unreachable, so RefreshAsync<T> proceeds to cache ANY type, registered or not, exactly as the pre-#975 code did. Positive-control decoupling argument (.claude/rules/testing.md, 'A mutant's positive control must not touch the mutated decision path'), verified against the fixture rather than assumed from either test's name: both green_test entries -- DistributedLookupCacheRefreshAsyncRegistryCheckTests975.RefreshAsync_RegisteredType_StillCachesNormally_NegativeControl and the pre-existing DistributedLookupCacheServiceTests.RefreshAsync_repopulates_cache_with_fresh_data -- call RefreshAsync<DCity>, and DCity carries [CacheLookup(TtlMinutes = 10, WarmOnStartup = true)] (DistributedLookupCacheTests.cs line 19), scanned into _registry by DistTestHelper.Create's `new DistributedLookupCacheService(distCache, new[] { typeof(DCity).Assembly }, options)` call (DistributedLookupCacheTests.cs lines 55-73; ScanAssemblies at DistributedLookupCacheService.cs line 106), so DCity is genuinely registered in both fixtures, not merely assumed to be from the '_RegisteredType_' name or the class-level negative-control comment. Both tests therefore DO reach the mutated line at DistributedLookupCacheService.cs line 383 for a registered type -- this is not the short-circuit (never-evaluated) form. It is the Invariant-result form instead: unmutated, `!_registry.ContainsKey(typeof(DCity))` evaluates `!true` -> `false`, so the early `return` is skipped; mutated, the condition is the literal `false`, so the early `return` is skipped identically -- the mutated and unmutated forms are provably equal for this specific (registered-type) input, the same category as dcext824's IsAssignableFrom argument in .claude/rules/testing.md step 3.

red_expected_assertion_patterns.WalkingTec.Mvvm.Core.Test.Cache.Distribu: Bug #975: RefreshAsync<T> must not write an unregistered

red_expected_assertion_patterns_observed: Captured from a real `python3 test/mutants/run_mutant.py --mutant lookupcache975-distributed-refreshasync-registry-guard-neutralize --trx-dir <scratch-dir>` invocation (Release build, stale demo.db under bin/ removed first) -- NOT retyped from terminal text. Read directly from the RED TRX file the run wrote (<scratch-dir>/lookupcache975-distributed-refreshasync-registry-guard-neutralize-red.trx) via xml.etree.ElementTree, the same parser run_mutant.py itself uses, extracting UnitTestResult/Output/ErrorInfo/Message: 'Assert.IsNull failed. Bug #975: RefreshAsync<T> must not write an unregistered (non-[CacheLookup]) type to the distributed cache -- even though such an entry would self-expire after the bounded 30-minute fallback TTL (unlike #944's immortal IMemoryCache entry), it must never be written in the first place.'. The dry run's own verdict on this first pass (before the pattern was filled in) was UNEXPECTED_RED against the PLACEHOLDER pattern, confirming the harness genuinely evaluated the mutant rather than short-circuiting; the result JSON (<scratch-dir>/lookupcache975-distributed-refreshasync-registry-guard-neutralize-result.json) records the same message verbatim. The chosen pattern intentionally excludes the parenthesized tail of the message (which contains '#944's' and other punctuation) to avoid unnecessary regex-escaping -- 'Bug #975: RefreshAsync<T> must not write an unregistered' alone is already unique to this guard's own assertion text, contains no regex metacharacters requiring escaping (no '.', '*', '(', ')', '[', ']', '\\', '^', '$', '+', '?', '{', '}', '|'), is confined to a single line (the message contains no embedded newline, sidestepping the '.*'-does-not-span-newlines-by-default pitfall), and does not match any PROBE_MESSAGES in run_mutant.py. After filling in the pattern above, two further independent invocations of `python3 test/mutants/run_mutant.py --mutant lookupcache975-distributed-refreshasync-registry-guard-neutralize` both reported 'VERDICT: KILLED' / 'GATE: PASS'.
